title: Security Notions for Truly Symmetric-Key UE and PRE
summary: For UE and PRE, good security notions require public-key encryption, while the best symmetric-only guarantees and whether fast primitives can improve on 2Enc remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For updatable encryption (UE) and proxy re-encryption (PRE), "good" security notions necessarily imply public-key encryption, but practitioners may be unwilling to incur the additional resources required for such strong cryptography. Characterize the best security notions achievable using only truly symmetric-key primitives; in particular, determine whether fast symmetric primitives can provide stronger security than Lehmann and Tackmann's 2Enc double-encryption protocol, which uses purely symmetric-key primitives.

scope.domain: Security notions for updatable encryption and proxy re-encryption in symmetric-key cryptography.
assumptions: Only truly symmetric-key primitives are used.
parameters: UE and PRE: the primitive classes under study
Fast symmetric primitives: candidate primitives whose security is evaluated
Lehmann and Tackmann's 2Enc: a purely symmetric-key double-encryption reference protocol
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the best security notions achievable for UE and PRE using only truly symmetric-key primitives, and determine whether fast symmetric primitives can provide stronger security than Lehmann and Tackmann's 2Enc double-encryption protocol.

progress.summary: The source presents this in its open-problems discussion, noting that "good" notions for UE and PRE necessarily imply public-key encryption. It then uses Lehmann and Tackmann's 2Enc as a purely symmetric-key double-encryption example and asks whether fast symmetric primitives can offer stronger security.
citation_labels: Navid Alamati et al., Symmetric Primitives with Structured Secrets
